item.title: Battle Drones browser RTS developed using AI coding agents and vibe coding
item.description:
Battle Drones browser RTS developed using AI coding agents and vibe coding

Battle Drones is a new Command & Conquer style Real Time Strategy (RTS) game developed as a “vibe coded” experiment. Built using AI coding agents, the browser-based game works on both mobile and desktop, featuring multiple play modes and support for both online and local audio-based multiplayer.

🔍 Overview

The project was built primarily using Claude Code, which contributed 321 commits across 12 major iterations. Development began in July using Claude Fable 5 and the Phaser 2D game framework, with later versions utilizing Claude Opus to regenerate sprites and improve visuals. The developer practiced “vibe coding,” reviewing almost none of the source code and building the game in TypeScript, a language they have rarely used.

⚙️ Key details

The game includes a variety of units and environmental features designed for strategic play. Units and structures are rendered as 3D models and include:

  • 9 buildings
  • 7 ground vehicles
  • 6 aerial vehicles
  • 3 infantry units
  • The Goliath: A giant mech equipped with laser eyes and arm cannons that can establish new bases

Gameplay mechanics include fog of war, specialized weapons for targeting ground or aerial units, crate drops with bonus resources, and in-game music that increases in intensity during combat. Players can progress through ranks and earn medals for achievements.

🧩 How it works

Battle Drones features several distinct modes of play and environmental variety:

Mode Description
Skirmish Red vs. blue combat on a rotationally symmetrical map
Last Stand A survival mode holding out against waves of enemies
AI vs. AI A spectator mode to watch different computer personalities compete
Agent vs. Agent A mode where two LLMs play the game against each other
Daily Op A recurring daily challenge

The game offers six maps across five biomes: temperate, desert, arctic, volcanic, and tropical. A random map generator is also included to provide new layouts. Players can select from different AI personalities, including Balanced, Rush, Air Swarm, Boom, Skyforce, and Ironclad.

🚀 Availability

Battle Drones is accessible via browser on mobile and desktop platforms. It supports online multiplayer and a unique local multiplayer system where two nearby devices use audio messages to synchronize game state. The game also includes “Mutators” that allow players to add extra rules or twists to their sessions.

#AIagents #GameDev #ClaudeCode #RTS #VibeCoding

Source: Battle Drones—a vibe coded RTS with audio-based multiplayer

item.title: Moku Brings Mobile Vibecoding Workspace for AI Agents to Multiple Platforms
item.description:
Moku Brings Mobile Vibecoding Workspace for AI Agents to Multiple Platforms

Moku, a pocket‑sized coding workspace for AI agents, is now available across iOS, macOS, Android, Linux and Windows, letting developers code from a phone or tablet with a full‑featured terminal experience.

🔍 Overview

  • Moku is a thoughtfully designed pocket workspace: a fast mobile terminal plus a coding workspace for your AI agents.
  • The goal is to make mobile vibecoding a daily habit, replacing hours spent tethered to a desk with a keyboard and mouse.
  • It is not traditional remote software; it delivers a delightfully crafted interaction, refined developer experience, polished UI, and exceptional performance.

🧩 How it Works

  • Runs locally in your browser; there are no real connections and no real commands.
  • Moku embeds Tailcat, the userspace networking tool from Tailscale’s open‑source stack.
    • Run tailcat --serve=22 on the host, paste the short token into Moku, and the two ends establish an encrypted peer‑to‑peer connection.
    • The link falls back to DERP relays only when necessary; there is no port forwarding, no relay VPS, no root required.
  • Native Mosh keeps the shell alive through Wi‑Fi ↔ 5G handoffs and elevator rides.
  • On iOS, the Dynamic Island and Lock Screen show your agent’s state through the mascot’s eyes.

⚙️ Key Features

  • A simulated server is already connected.
  • Pick a coding app, expand a project, and drop into a conversation right on the same page.
  • Moku lists every open pane at the top of the drawer with its current task; you can peek in read‑only or take the keyboard with a single tap.
  • On connect, Moku scans the host for on‑disk projects and sessions from 12+ coding CLIs: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qoder, Trae, Kimi, Grok, MiniMax Code and more.
  • Selecting a project and tapping its session reopens it inside a real terminal with full context.
  • Moku’s Rust core parses ANSI at 2.1× the throughput of common emulators and paints a 10 MiB log burst in about 0.3 s.
  • Multiple agents can run side by side on one host (e.g., Herdr runs several agents such as pi exploring, grok implementing, codex chasing a root cause).

🚀 Availability

  • Free on every platform.
  • iOS: available on the App Store and via a public TestFlight beta.
  • macOS: ships through TestFlight.
  • Android: Universal APK and per‑ABI builds downloadable from GitHub Releases.
  • Linux & Windows: Native packages (.deb / tarball for Linux, Windows installer) on GitHub Releases.
  • Not listed in mainland China yet — the App Store link requires a non‑CN Apple ID.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Classic mobile SSH clients (e.g., Termius, Blink Shell, Prompt) were designed for emergency sysadmin commands; Moku was built from day one for mobile vibecoding and AI agents.
  • Zero‑config private networking works without public IPs or router configuration.
  • One‑tap resume for Claude Code, Codex and other agents enables developers to code anywhere, turning a phone into a usable development terminal.

#Moku #AIAgents #MobileCoding #Vibecoding

Source: Moku — Pocket terminal & coding workspace for the AI-coding era

item.title: Free Vibe Coding Workshop Series Teaches AI-Driven Software Creation
item.description:
Free Vibe Coding Workshop Series Teaches AI-Driven Software Creation

WIT // HSV and ARC are hosting a free, three‑part Vibe Coding Workshop Series that shows participants how to turn natural‑language prompts into working software using AI‑powered code generators.

🔍 Overview

  • Hands‑on, immersive workshops (not lectures) that guide AI tools to generate, iterate, and improve code.
  • Series consists of three 2‑hour modules for a total of 6 hours of instruction.
  • Open to professionals, students, educators, creators, and curious minds.

🧩 How it works

  • Vibe coding lets you build functional software simply by describing intent in natural language.
  • Participants will explore cloud‑native AI app builders to turn ideas into interactive applications without writing code manually.
Platform Role
Lovable Cloud‑native AI app builder
Bolt.new Cloud‑native AI app builder
Google AI Studio Cloud‑native AI app builder
  • The curriculum advances from browser‑based low‑code platforms and AI agents, to cloud development environments with controlled code customization, and finally to fully local setups with open‑source tools and LLM architectures.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Free to attend – no cost for participants.
  • Open to all – no prerequisites or prior coding experience required.
  • Bring your own laptop – required for the fully immersive experience.
  • Certificate of Completion – awarded to attendees who complete all three workshops (a valuable addition to a resume or LinkedIn profile).
  • Workshop schedule:
    • Prompt to Prototype – 10/8
    • Collaborative Cloud Coding – 10/22
    • Owning Your Code – 11/12
  • Spots are limited and fill fast.

🚀 Availability

  • Register now to secure a spot; the event is free and open to everyone.
  • 👉 For more information on the three‑part workshop series, click here.

💡 Why it matters

  • The barrier between having an idea and building something that works is disappearing.
  • Natural language is becoming a development interface thanks to AI‑powered platforms and coding agents.
  • The next generation of builders will be defined by the ability to clearly describe what should be built, not by years of programming experience.
  • Vibe coding is changing who can create software.

#AIWorkshop #VibeCoding #LowCode #AItools

Source: VIBE CODING ESSENTIALS - Workshop 1 : Prompt to Prototype
